attribute: lease / agreement / well identifier on Native American records
what_was_swept: all five ONRR bulk files held locally: monthly_revenue, calendar_year_revenue, fiscal_year_revenue, fiscal_year_disbursements, monthly_production
evidence: No ONRR bulk file carries a lease, agreement, tract or well column for ANY land class, and the publisher states: 'For all Native American land, the federal government only releases natural resource extraction and revenue information in aggregate. Specific data on Native American revenues are confidential and proprietary.'

attribute: state / county / FIPS on Native American records
evidence: 0 of 9,238 Native rows carry any geography, against 99.8% of Federal rows in the same file. Re-measured on every run of script 83.
No ONRR file has a tribe-name field at all. 'Osage' appears zero times across all of them, despite the Osage mineral estate having exactly one owner.

837 Native American rows, land class x land category x commodity x volume. Held raw: with no lease, geography or entity there is nothing to attach a volume to, and volume x price is a model, not a measurement.

attribute: lease / tract / agreement / well identifiers for Indian minerals
evidence: NIOGEMS is an internal BIA system on the order of 50 tribal users across 8 reservations. No public interface or extract was located. The niogems_* columns are empty BY CONSTRUCTION so that access, if ever granted, is a merge and not a rebuild. Partnership target, never a cited source.

attribute: per-lease and per-tract records of the Osage Mineral Estate
evidence: The Agency states it administers leasing of the 1.45 million-acre estate; it publishes the estate's extent, not its leases.

publisher: North Dakota Dept. of Mineral Resources
attribute: mineral ownership (trust vs fee) on wells
what_was_swept: DMR free well search field list
evidence: No DMR field states trust vs fee mineral ownership. Trust/fee is a Tax Commissioner construct and is FRACTIONAL, not binary - each spacing unit carries a Trust Ratio by mineral acreage. The strings TRUST and INDIAN in DMR data are lease, well and operator NAMES and must never be parsed as ownership. The complete Well Index is subscription-gated.

publisher: Montana Board of Oil and Gas Conservation
evidence: Location and well identity only; no mineral-ownership field. Same conclusion as North Dakota.

attribute: executed tribal mineral leases filed as exhibits
what_was_swept: EDGAR full-text search for the Navajo/Hopi lease language, and the Westmoreland exhibit index
evidence: Two instruments retrieved: the Crow Tribal Lands Coal Lease (EX-10.51) and Peabody's FY2010 10-K describing three Navajo/Hopi coal leases. This is the only route found to a tribal lease INSTRUMENT. www.sec.gov returns HTTP 403 without a declared User-Agent; that is an access rule, not an absence.

attribute: royalty rate on tribal coal leases
evidence: Peabody states tribal rates are 'generally based upon a percentage of the gross realization' and gives no number; the 12.5%/8.0% rates in the same filing are FEDERAL leases. Westmoreland's lease gives 6.5% capped at 12.5% but no tonnage. Rate x tonnage is a model and is refused in both cases.
